value.answer: For most adults, short-term use looks safe. The NIH says it appears safe for most people, and UC Davis says it's typically well tolerated at low doses when taken for the shortest time, which they count as one to two months. Long-term safety is less clear. A new American Heart Association abstract from November 2025 linked a year or more of use in people with chronic insomnia to more heart failure diagnoses and deaths, but it's preliminary, not peer-reviewed, and can't prove cause. Some experts think poor sleep may be the real driver. Sources also disagree on dose and time limits, and higher doses can cause drowsiness the next day. It can interact with other medicines, and if you're older, have had fractures, or have a long-running sleep problem, check with a doctor or pharmacist before starting.
